messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Insulin glargine is a long-acting insulin used to treat type 1 and type 2 diabetes in certain patients to improve and maintain blood glucose levels. Insulin glargine is a man-made form of human insulin that is used once daily to provide a base level of insulin that keeps working for 24 hours or longer.
Insulin glargine is available under the brand names Lantus, Basaglar, Toujeo, Semglee, and Rezvoglar. Langlara is an interchangeable biosimilar to Lantus that was FDA-approved on May 4, 2026.
Rezvoglar, Lantus, Langlara, Semglee, and Toujeo are FDA-approved to be used for use in adult and pediatric patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Basasglar is FDA-approved to be used by adults for type 2 diabetes and also for adults and pediatric patients with type 1 diabetes. In patients with type 1 diabetes, insulin glargine must be used together with a short-acting insulin.
Triplet: ["Insulin glargine", "approved for use in", "adult patients with type 1 diabetes"]

The relation 'approved for use in' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject entity approved for use in the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'are supported by': The subject entity are supported by the object entity.
B. 'has location': The subject entity is located at the address specified by the object entity.
C. 'used in population': The subject drug is used in or approved for the patient population or age group specified by the object entity.
D. 'has dosage form': The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
E. 'includes': The activity or intervention specified by the subject entity comprises the component or practice specified by the object entity.
